candidates.explanation: Labels behavior is coherently colocated under one module root, with route-specific glue in app. The design avoids an application layer and repository port, uses direct RSC reads, an authenticated cacheable GET for browser reads, and top-level Server Actions for writes. Identity is server-derived with scoped predicates and RLS. Provider rows and mappings remain private, with explicit browser-safe surfaces.

The feature root contains the core labels behavior while app holds route and form glue. Its concrete repository avoids a speculative provider port, but the CRUD service adds some potentially forwarding operation-level indirection. Read and write channels, server-derived authentication, RLS, validation, and private row mapping are otherwise clear. The generic lib bucket violates the final negative criterion.

Labels code is distributed across horizontal domain, data, adapters, client-cache, and UI roots rather than colocated beneath one labels root. It correctly avoids a repository port and application operations. RSC and GET reads use a server-only read entry, browser reads remain GET-based, and writes are Server Actions. Authentication, scoped authorization, private row mapping, and client/server separation are coherent.

The proposal spreads labels across many horizontal roots instead of one capability root. It also introduces a repository port and separate forwarding use-case file for every simple CRUD operation. The runtime channels, server-derived identity, RLS and ownership checks, and private provider mapping are strong. Per-operation wrappers and the generic use-cases/shared bucket trigger negative criteria.
